strengths.point: The eps trend has been rising for 6 years in a row.

weaknesses.point: Operating cash flow is negative while the company books a profit.
The share price has run ahead of the fundamentals.
Operating profit converts poorly into cash.
Costs are rising faster than sales.
Receivables tie up a lot of cash.
Inventory tie up a lot of cash.
Working capital absorbs a very large slice of the year's sales.

P/E is expensive against the sector median.

Institutional money has been flowing out.

opportunities.point: Buying below the model's intrinsic value leaves room for a re-rating.

opportunities.evidence: CWIP 9 Cr -> 13 Cr (44.4%) as of Mar 2026

opportunities.point: The price embeds less growth than the company has actually delivered.

opportunities.point: P/B is cheaper than the sector median.

threats.point: The business consumed cash from operations in the latest year.
Profit is growing while operating cash flow is shrinking - an earnings-quality gap.
threats.evidence: Net profit 15 -> 22 Cr (Mar 2026) but operating cash flow 15 Cr (Mar 2025) -> -8 Cr (Mar 2026)

threats.point: Institutional holding keeps falling - the selling has not stopped.
threats.evidence: Institutional Holding trend (quarterly): Decreasing for 6 quarters

threats.point: A premium multiple versus peers can unwind quickly if growth slips.
Promoter selling is a warning about insider conviction.
Both foreign and domestic institutions have been reducing.
threats.evidence: FII -2.27 pp, DII -2.86 pp over the recent quarters

threats.point: A price that has outrun earnings needs the growth to catch up or it de-rates.
Small size brings liquidity and volatility risk.
Historically weak quarters (Mar) are still in the cycle.
